title: Custom Derive Macros
concept: Custom derive macros let you write your own code generators — write once, apply to hundreds of types with a single #[derive(MyTrait)] annotation.
why: When standard derives don't cover your use case, custom derives let you encode your project's patterns as reusable macros — DRY at the type-system level.
tips: Custom derives are for PROJECT-LEVEL patterns — not one-off implementations
Derive macros operate on type definitions — they have access to field names and types
Test your derive with multiple types — empty struct, single field, many fields, generics
Attribute annotations (#[validate(...)]) let callers customize derive behavior per field
common_mistakes: Writing a custom derive for something that can be a generic function — derives are for type-level code gen
Not handling generic types in the derive — #[derive(MyTrait)] on MyType[T] should work
Forgetting to handle edge cases: zero-field structs, unit enums, tuple structs
